props.title: Time After Time
props.initialSlug: H.G. Wells chases Jack the Ripper through time

sections.content: Time After Time (1979) brilliantly combines H.G. Wells' time travel concepts with fish-out-of-water comedy and serial killer thrills. Nicholas Meyer's directorial debut pairs Malcolm McDowell's charmingly proper H.G. Wells with David Warner's sinister Jack the Ripper in a chase through 1979 San Francisco. The film established key time travel tropes later seen in Back to the Future (1985) and Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure (1989) - particularly the culture shock of historical figures encountering modern technology and social norms. Meyer's clever script uses Wells' own literary themes about technological progress and human nature to critique contemporary society.

sections.content: The late 1970s and early 1980s saw a fascinating surge in romantic time travel films that balanced sci-fi concepts with human drama. Somewhere in Time (1980) used time travel as a vehicle for sweeping romance, while Time Bandits (1981) injected Terry Gilliam's signature weird humor into historical adventures. These films paved the way for more effects-driven time travel blockbusters like The Terminator (1984) and Back to the Future (1985), which would define the genre for decades to come.

What sets Time After Time apart is its ingenious use of real historical figures and social commentary. The film's fish-out-of-water elements work both for comedy and critique - Wells' horror at modern violence serves as pointed commentary on "progress," while his romance with Mary Steenburgen's liberated bank teller challenges his Victorian sensibilities. Meyer would later bring similar historical playfulness to Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country (1991). SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Time Travel Cinema

sections.content: The success of Time After Time helped establish key narrative rules for time travel films that persist today. The idea of a historical figure struggling with modern technology became a genre staple, seen in everything from Les Visiteurs (1993) to Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure (1989). The film's careful attention to paradox and causality influenced later works like 12 Monkeys (1995) and Looper (2012), while its blend of genres showed how time travel could enhance different types of stories beyond pure science fiction.
